newsitem.title: USA: Owens-Illinois to call $400 mln of notes.
newsitem.headline: Owens-Illinois to call $400 mln of notes.

text.p: Owens-Illinois Inc said on Friday that it will call for redemption $400 million in principal of its senior subordinated notes as part of a refinancing.

Owens-Illinois also completed the closings of its offerings of 14,750,000 shares of common stock, $300 million principal amount of 7.85 percent senior notes due May 15, 2004, and $300 million principal amount of 8.10 percent senior notes due May 15, 2007, the company said.
Also, Owens-Illinois increased its bank credit facility to $3.0 billion from $1.8 billion.

Owens-Illinois said all of the $250 million of 10-1/4 percent senior subordinated notes due 1999 will be redeemed at a redemption price of 100 percent of the principal amount plus accrued interest to the redemption date of June 16, 1997.

All of the $150 million of 10-1/2 percent senior subordinated notes due 2002 will be redeemed at a redemption price of 105.25 percent of the principal amount plus accrued interest to the redemption date, Owens-Illinois said.
Redemption will be funded by borrowings under the company's bank credit facility, Owens-Illinois said.

Also, Owens-Illinois said it has obtained consents and tenders from registered holders of the 11 percent senior debentures representing more than 95 percent of the $1 billion in debentures. The tender offer will expire May 22, 1997, unless extended, the company said.

The refinancing plan also contemplates the redemption, at the company's option, of an aggregate of $550 million principal amount of the company's remaining senior subordinated notes starting August 1, 1997.
The redemption of such notes will be made at the discretion of the company, depending on prevailing market and economic conditions, Owens-Illinois said.
